A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PersonalAlign work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original AndroidIntent evaluations, HIM-Agent comparisons, component ablations, and supplementary proactive-model results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds a weighting ablation and explicit annotation-score sensitivity plots.

M1.justification: HIM-Agent retains the same streaming aggregation, execution-based preference filter, and state-based routine filter. Their procedures, inputs, memory representations, and Equations 5–7 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same AndroidIntent coverage: 775 preference interactions and 215 routine interactions derived from 91 users' records. V2's benchmark-scale table and discussion of other platforms and languages do not establish additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding performance tables retain the same comparator sets, including supplementary proactive models. V2's appendix shortens UI-TARS-1.5-7B to UI-TARS-7B, but its result tables still identify UI-TARS-1.5; no comparator replacement is established.

E3.justification: V2 Figure 6 adds a 'w/o Weight' experimental control to the proactive ablations. The main split, offline evaluation, metrics' stated computations, and selected hyperparameters remain unchanged. CER is relabeled CSR without a documented computational change.

E4.justification: V2 extends the proactive ablation with 'w/o Weight' and adds Figure 8 comparing Qscore distributions under three weight settings. These provide additional evidence beyond v1's existing qualitative statement about alternative weights; other ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's additional sensitivity histograms do not introduce uncertainty estimation or a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds plotted outcomes for 'w/o Weight,' three weight-dependent score distributions, and benchmark-scale comparisons in Table 2. Matched performance tables retain their numerical values, including HIM-Agent's 42.3 execution score and 49.0% false-alarm rate.

T1.justification: The task definitions and mathematical formulations in Equations 1–10 are retained, including the appendix formulations of alternative agent settings. No new proof, derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same PersonalAlign task, AndroidIntent benchmark, and HIM-Agent contributions. The abstract's claimed 15.7% execution and 7.3% proactive improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly argues that the annotation pipeline transfers across platforms and languages with minimal adaptation and emphasizes comparative benchmark breadth. Appendix A.2 explicitly interprets the weight plots as robustness evidence. Existing limitations and privacy discussion are retained.

D1.justification: V2 changes the repository address, specifies the GPT-5.1 snapshot and QwenVL-Max endpoint alias, identifies student annotators in China and their compensation standard, and documents the plotted sensitivity weights. These are disclosures, not evidence that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Galaxy, OS-ATLAS, and additional memory and robotics work, while removing GUI-Explorer, HiconAgent, and several general multimodal references. Related-work prose and benchmark-scale positioning change, but the central distinction from prior personalization and memory approaches remains.

P1.justification: Dataset statistics move from Appendix A into Section 4.3, and the privacy discussion becomes 'Ethical considerations.' V2 also edits related-work prose, affiliations, and metric terminology, reorganizes appendix labels, and adds an AI-writing-assistance disclosure. Most exposition remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds a benchmark-scale table and sensitivity figure, expands and redraws the proactive-ablation chart, and relocates the dataset-statistics figure into the main text. Execution tables gain CSR labels and upward arrows; other diagrams receive limited label and layout edits.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful ablation and sensitivity evidence and improves reproducibility disclosures through model identifiers and annotator information. Renaming CER to CSR better matches the retained higher-is-better scores. These are limited gains: core results remain unchanged, the new 'w/o Weight' control lacks procedural explanation, and cross-platform and language applicability remains untested.
